scope: Proposition 13.4 (Tests away from coincidence) of the manuscript “Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1 <= q < 4” (preprints/Square-lattice-FK-interfaces-and-nested-loops-for-1-leq-q-lt-4-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d2ffa94ece599e88), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 83. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For x > 0 beyond these localization bounds, the quantities Mt(x) = xg′ t(x) gt(x) − WH t !h (13.5) satisfy the approximate martingale identities between arbitrary causal stops on the segment. Tests may include the entire earlier exploration history of finitely many targets. The errors tend to zero after the mesh limit. The assertion concerns the averaged identities for this history law, not a uniform assertion over all deterministic mazes.
